current_law_statement: Sessions reviewed: through the 2025-2026 session, MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026 (legislature.mi.gov banner, confirmed on 2026-08-21). MCL 15.234 taken from the Kevin-supplied official legislature.mi.gov print (source_docs/MI_mcl_15.234_2026-08-20.txt); its history ends Am. 2020 PA 38, so no 2024-2026 amendment touches the fee section. MCL 15.235 (response/appeal timing) and MCL 408.934 (minimum wage, the (1)(b) delegation instrument) opened directly on legislature.mi.gov on 2026-08-21 under the same currency banner (site served with an incomplete TLS certificate chain; content fetched from the official host). A web search for 2024-2026 enacted amendments to the FOIA fee sections found none. Michigan runs a single FOIA fee regime for all public bodies - state, county, and municipal alike (MCL 15.232 definition of public body); there is no separate state-agency uniform fee schedule and no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local bodies. Guidance layer (AG FOIA materials, DTMB model form and summary) restates the statute; the DTMB standard itemization form is optional for non-state bodies, which may create their own compliant form.

resolutions.unit: USD per sheet (8-1/2 x 11 or 8-1/2 x 14 paper)
resolutions.source_language: The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper. A public body shall utilize the most economical means available for making copies of public records, including using double-sided printing, if cost saving and available.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Ceiling, not a set rate: also bounded by actual total incremental duplication cost (labor excluded and separately capped); most economical means incl. double-sided printing required. City sets the operative rate at or under 10 cents.

resolutions.unit: USD per sheet (8-1/2 x 11 or 8-1/2 x 14 paper, any print type)
resolutions.source_language: The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper. A public body shall utilize the most economical means available for making copies of public records, including using double-sided printing, if cost saving and available.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: The statute draws no B&W/color distinction: the 10-cents-per-sheet cap covers all paper copies on letter/legal paper, color included, and the actual-incremental-cost limit still applies. Color on nonstandard-size paper falls to the actual-cost clause (see dup.oversized.rate).

resolutions.value: actual total incremental cost of necessary duplication or publication, not including labor
resolutions.source_language: For paper copies of public records provided to the requestor, the actual total incremental cost of necessary duplication or publication, not including labor. The cost of paper copies shall be calculated as a total cost per sheet of paper and shall be itemized and noted in a manner that expresses both the cost per sheet and the number of sheets provided. The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: The 10-cent cap is textually limited to 8-1/2x11 and 8-1/2x14 paper; copies on any other size remain governed by (1)(d)'s opening clause - actual total incremental cost, excluding labor, itemized per sheet. New rule MI-9001 captures this.

resolutions.value: actual incremental cost of duplication or publication (media at actual most-economical cost; labor at capped rates)
resolutions.source_language: Subject to subsections (2), (3), (4), (5), and (9), the fee must be limited to actual mailing costs, and to the actual incremental cost of duplication or publication including labor, the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14. Except as otherwise provided in this act, if the public body estimates or charges a fee in accordance with this act, the total fee must not exceed the sum of the following components:
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No specialty schedule (photos, maps, transcripts) exists; specialty reproduction resolves through the 6-component actual-incremental-cost structure. Records whose sale or copy fee is set by another statute are carved out of § 15.234 entirely by subsection (10) (MI-0052).

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No graduated page bands: MCL 15.234 sets a single flat per-sheet ceiling (10 cents on letter/legal) with no volume tiers; a city may adopt tiers beneath the ceiling but the state supplies none. Searched the full FOIA act MCL 15.231-15.246 (official print of 15.234 complete through PA 91 of 2026 supplied; 15.235 opened on legislature.mi.gov, same currency banner); Michigan has no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local public bodies; AG FOIA guidance and DTMB model materials restate the statute.

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No free-page allowance per request. The $20.00 no-charge amount in § 15.234(2)(a)-(b) is a dollar-denominated waiver limited to indigent-affidavit requesters and designated P&A nonprofits, not a page allowance; website-posted records are exempt only from (1)(b) redaction charges (MI-0046). Searched the full FOIA act MCL 15.231-15.246 (official print of 15.234 complete through PA 91 of 2026 supplied; 15.235 opened on legislature.mi.gov, same currency banner); Michigan has no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local public bodies; AG FOIA guidance and DTMB model materials restate the statute.

resolutions.value: hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of searching for, locating, and examining the public records
resolutions.unit: USD per hour (formula ceiling, no fixed number)
resolutions.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of searching for, locating, and examining the public records in the particular instance regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor. Labor costs under this subdivision shall be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Formula ceiling, applies regardless of who actually performs the labor; chargeable at all only through the § 15.234(3) unreasonably-high-costs gate (MI-0045); up to +50% fringe multiplier (MI-0041); 15-minute increments rounded down.

resolutions.value: hourly wage of lowest-paid capable employee; contracted redaction labor <= 6 x state minimum hourly wage ($13.73 from Jan 1, 2026, so <= $82.38/hour during 2026)
resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws § 15.234(1)(b); Mich. Comp. Laws § 408.934(1)
resolutions.source_language: For services performed by an employee of the public body, the public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of separating and deleting exempt information from nonexempt information in the particular instance as provided in section 14, regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor. [...] Total labor costs calculated under this subdivision for contracted labor costs must not exceed an amount equal to 6 times the state minimum hourly wage rate determined under section 4 of the improved workforce opportunity wage act, 2018 PA 337, MCL 408.934.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Delegation followed: the 6x contracted-labor cap references MCL 408.934, opened - $12.48 from Feb 21, 2025; $13.73 from Jan 1, 2026; $15.00 from Jan 1, 2027; CPI-adjusted thereafter (new rule MI-9002). Contracted labor usable only when no capable employee exists, FOIA-coordinator determined case-by-case, contractor named on itemization. No charge for re-redacting a record already redacted and still in possession (MI-0032). Subject to the (3) gate and 15-minute increments.

resolutions.value: hourly wage of the public body's lowest-paid employee capable of necessary duplication or publication
resolutions.source_language: The public body shall not charge more than the hourly wage of its lowest-paid employee capable of necessary duplication or publication in the particular instance, regardless of whether that person is available or who actually performs the labor. Labor costs under this subdivision may be estimated and charged in time increments of the public body's choosing; however, all partial time increments shall be rounded down.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Michigan FOIA has no separate programming/data-extraction fee category; making digital copies and transferring digital records is (1)(e) duplication labor under the lowest-paid-capable-employee ceiling, in time increments of the body's choosing rounded down. Not subject to the § 15.234(3) gate (which covers only search/examination/review/separation).

resolutions.source_language: A fee as described in subsection (1) shall not be charged for the cost of search, examination, review, and the deletion and separation of exempt from nonexempt information as provided in section 14 unless failure to charge a fee would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request in the particular instance, and the public body specifically identifies the nature of these unreasonably high costs.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Gate, not a numeric threshold: search/examination/review/redaction labor is chargeable only if failure to charge would result in unreasonably high costs to the public body because of the nature of the request, with the nature of those costs specifically identified. No page/hour trigger and no paper-only scope. Duplication labor (1)(e) is outside this gate. Separate absolute gate: no fees or deposits at all until procedures/guidelines/public summary are published (MI-0050); website-posted records exempt from (1)(b) charges (MI-0046).

resolutions.unit: percent of the applicable labor charge (capped at actual fringe-benefit cost; overtime excluded from the fringe calculation)
resolutions.source_language: The public body may also add up to 50% to the applicable labor charge amount to cover or partially cover the cost of fringe benefits if it clearly notes the percentage multiplier used to account for benefits in the detailed itemization described in subsection (4). Subject to the 50% limitation, the public body shall not charge more than the actual cost of fringe benefits, and overtime wages shall not be used in calculating the cost of fringe benefits.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Fringe-benefit multiplier only - no general overhead surcharge is permitted. Multiplier must be noted on the itemization. Overtime wages excluded from labor costs unless stipulated by the requester (MI-0042). Exception: a fringe multiplier above 50% (up to actual costs) is allowed only in the website-then-paper scenario of § 15.234(5).

resolutions.unit: minutes (search (1)(a) and redaction (1)(b) labor; partial increments rounded down). Duplication labor (1)(e): increments of the body's choosing, rounded down.
resolutions.source_language: Labor costs under this subdivision shall be estimated and charged in increments of 15 minutes or more, with all partial time increments rounded down.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Identical 15-minute-or-more increment sentence appears in both (1)(a) and (1)(b); rounding is always down. (1)(e) leaves the increment to the body but keeps round-down.

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No free-labor-hours allowance per request. Michigan instead gates labor charging entirely on the § 15.234(3) unreasonably-high-costs test, and gives the first $20.00 free only to indigent/P&A-nonprofit requesters - neither is an hours allowance. Searched the full FOIA act MCL 15.231-15.246 (official print of 15.234 complete through PA 91 of 2026 supplied; 15.235 opened on legislature.mi.gov, same currency banner); Michigan has no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local public bodies; AG FOIA guidance and DTMB model materials restate the statute.

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No per-requestor periodic free personnel time (no TX Gov't Code § 552.275 analog). The only requestor-ledger mechanism in the act is the prior-nonpayer increased-deposit regime of § 15.234(11)-(12) and the twice-per-calendar-year limit on the indigent $20 discount in § 15.234(2)(a)(i). Searched the full FOIA act MCL 15.231-15.246 (official print of 15.234 complete through PA 91 of 2026 supplied; 15.235 opened on legislature.mi.gov, same currency banner); Michigan has no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local public bodies; AG FOIA guidance and DTMB model materials restate the statute.

resolutions.unit: no dollar/hours threshold - itemization required for ANY fee estimated or charged
resolutions.source_language: A public body's procedures and guidelines must include the use of a standard form for detailed itemization of any fee amount in its responses to written requests under this act. The detailed itemization must clearly list and explain the allowable charges for each of the 6 fee components listed under subsection (1) that compose the total fee used for estimating or charging purposes.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Michigan does not set a dollar trigger: the standard-form detailed itemization of the 6 fee components is mandatory whenever a fee is estimated or charged (effectively a $0 threshold). A deposit demand (only above a $50 estimate) must additionally include the itemization and a nonbinding best-efforts timeframe estimate (§ 15.234(8)).

resolutions.unit: days from the requester's receipt of the deposit notice (notice deemed received 3 days after sending; stated due date must be 48 days after the notice is sent)
resolutions.source_language: If a deposit that is required under subsection (8) or (11) is not received by the public body within 45 days from receipt by the requesting person of the notice that a deposit is required, and if the requesting person has not filed an appeal of the deposit amount pursuant to section 10a, the request shall be considered abandoned by the requesting person and the public body is no longer required to fulfill the request. Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) is considered received 3 days after it is sent, regardless of the means of transmission. Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) must include notice of the date by which the deposit must be received, which date is 48 days after the date the notice is sent.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Applies only when a deposit is required under (8) or (11): nonpayment within 45 days of receipt = request abandoned, unless a § 15.240a deposit-amount appeal was filed. No response window exists for a fee estimate that carries no deposit demand. Corresponds to existing rule MI-0059 per the provenance note.

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No revised-estimate trigger when actual cost exceeds the estimate. The 105% figure in § 15.234(11)(a) is an eligibility condition for the prior-nonpayer 100% deposit on a LATER request (final fee for the prior request was not more than 105% of its estimate), not a revision-notice threshold for the current request - the prior snippet's percentages are rejected for this item. Searched the full FOIA act MCL 15.231-15.246 (official print of 15.234 complete through PA 91 of 2026 supplied; 15.235 opened on legislature.mi.gov, same currency banner); Michigan has no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local public bodies; AG FOIA guidance and DTMB model materials restate the statute.

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No estimate validity period. The only statutory lifetimes are deposit-linked: the 45-day abandonment window (§ 15.234(14)) and the 365-day expiry of the prior-nonpayer increased-deposit authority (§ 15.234(12)(c)). Searched the full FOIA act MCL 15.231-15.246 (official print of 15.234 complete through PA 91 of 2026 supplied; 15.235 opened on legislature.mi.gov, same currency banner); Michigan has no administrative FOIA fee rules binding local public bodies; AG FOIA guidance and DTMB model materials restate the statute.

resolutions.unit: USD (good-faith deposit permitted only if the entire fee estimate or charge exceeds $50.00)
resolutions.source_language: In either the public body's initial response or subsequent response as described under section 5(2)(d), the public body may require a good-faith deposit from the person requesting information before providing the public records to the requestor if the entire fee estimate or charge authorized under this section exceeds $50.00, based on a good-faith calculation of the total fee described in subsection (4).
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Statutory statewide trigger; must be based on a good-faith calculation of the total fee under (4), demanded in the initial or extended § 15.235(2) response, and is barred entirely until the body's procedures/guidelines/summary are published (MI-0050). A deposit is a fee (§ 15.234(13)).

resolutions.unit: percent of the total estimated fee (deposit must not exceed 1/2)
resolutions.source_language: Subject to subsection (10), the deposit must not exceed 1/2 of the total estimated fee, and a public body's request for a deposit must include a detailed itemization as required under subsection (4).
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Exception: up to 100% of the estimated fee for a subsequent request from an individual who left a prior fulfilled request unpaid, only while all six § 15.234(11)(a)-(f) conditions hold; the authority ends on proof of payment, later payment in full, or 365 days after the unpaid request (§ 15.234(12), MI-0057).

resolutions.source_language: In either the public body's initial response or subsequent response as described under section 5(2)(d), the public body may require a good-faith deposit from the person requesting information before providing the public records to the requestor if the entire fee estimate or charge authorized under this section exceeds $50.00, based on a good-faith calculation of the total fee described in subsection (4).
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.manual_verification: Confirm via AG guidance or case law that release may be conditioned on payment of the full remaining balance, not only the statutory deposit; § 15.234(11)(c) ('made available to the individual, subject to payment') and (13) (a deposit is a fee) support but do not expressly state a full-payment gate.
resolutions.notes: Express statutory gate: a good-faith deposit may be required 'before providing the public records to the requestor' (estimate > $50). Conditioning final release on payment of the balance is the standard reading - (11)(c) describes prior records 'made available to the individual, subject to payment' - but the act states the gate expressly only for deposits.

resolutions.unit: days (required deposit unpaid after receipt of notice -> request considered abandoned; body relieved of duty to fulfill)
resolutions.source_language: If a deposit that is required under subsection (8) or (11) is not received by the public body within 45 days from receipt by the requesting person of the notice that a deposit is required, and if the requesting person has not filed an appeal of the deposit amount pursuant to section 10a, the request shall be considered abandoned by the requesting person and the public body is no longer required to fulfill the request.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Terminal consequence (abandonment), tolled only by a § 15.240a deposit-amount appeal. Prior-debt consequence: an individual who never paid a prior fulfilled request may face an up-to-100% deposit on subsequent requests for up to 365 days (§ 15.234(11)-(12)).

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws § 15.234(8), (14); Mich. Comp. Laws § 15.235(2)
resolutions.source_language: The response must also contain a best efforts estimate by the public body regarding the time frame it will take the public body to comply with the law in providing the public records to the requestor. The time frame estimate is nonbinding upon the public body, but the public body shall provide the estimate in good faith and strive to be reasonably accurate and to provide the public records in a manner based on this state's public policy under section 1 and the nature of the request in the particular instance. Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) is considered received 3 days after it is sent, regardless of the means of transmission. Notice of a deposit requirement under subsection (8) or (11) must include notice of the date by which the deposit must be received, which date is 48 days after the date the notice is sent.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: The 5-business-day (+ one 10-business-day extension) response clock of § 15.235(2) is NOT tolled by a deposit - the deposit demand is itself made in the (2) response, and § 15.235 (opened at legislature.mi.gov, complete through PA 91 of 2026, history ends 2020 PA 36) contains no deposit-tolling provision. After a deposit is demanded, production is governed only by the nonbinding best-efforts timeframe estimate of § 15.234(8). Mechanics: notice deemed received 3 days after sending; due date stated as 48 days after sending; terminal abandonment 45 days after receipt (MI-0059/MI-0060).

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No overrun re-issue rule: nothing requires a revised estimate or blocks collection when actual cost exceeds the estimate, and no window restarts. Closest provisions: any charged amount must be itemized on the standard form (§ 15.234(4)), and a final fee exceeding 105% of the estimate disqualifies the body from using the prior-nonpayer deposit tool on that individual's later request (§ 15.234(11)(a)). Except as otherwise provided in this act, if the public body estimates or charges a fee in accordance with this act, the total fee must not exceed the sum of the following components:

resolutions.value: actual and most reasonably economical cost of the nonpaper physical media
resolutions.source_language: For public records provided to the requestor on any form of nonpaper physical media, the actual and most reasonably economical cost of the nonpaper physical media.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Requester may stipulate nonpaper media, e-mail, or other electronic delivery in lieu of paper; the subdivision does not apply if the body lacks the technological capability for the stipulated media. Transfer labor is separately chargeable under (1)(e).

resolutions.value: actual cost of mailing, in a reasonably economical and justifiable manner
resolutions.source_language: The actual cost of mailing, if any, for sending the public records in a reasonably economical and justifiable manner. The public body shall not charge more for expedited shipping or insurance unless specifically stipulated by the requestor, but may otherwise charge for the least expensive form of postal delivery confirmation when mailing public records.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: No expedited shipping or insurance charge unless the requester stipulates it; the least expensive form of postal delivery confirmation may be charged. No statutory charge for e-mail delivery or pickup (only the 6 components may be charged).

resolutions.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws §§ 15.231-15.246 (searched; no provision found)

MCL 15.233 obliges a public body to furnish certified copies on request, but § 15.234(1) caps the total fee at the sum of the 6 enumerated components, none of which is a certification surcharge; records whose copy fee is fixed by another statute (e.g., vital records) sit outside § 15.234 via subsection (10). resolutions.source_language: A search for a public record may be conducted or copies of public records may be furnished without charge or at a reduced charge if the public body determines that a waiver or reduction of the fee is in the public interest because searching for or furnishing copies of the public record can be considered as primarily benefiting the general public. A public record search shall be made and a copy of a public record shall be furnished without charge for the first $20.00 of the fee for each request by either of the following:
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Two grounds: (1) discretionary public-interest waiver/reduction where disclosure primarily benefits the general public (soft standard, MI-0044); (2) mandatory first-$20.00-free per request for indigent-affidavit requesters (ineligible if discounted twice that calendar year by the same body or requesting in conjunction with paid outside parties) and for state-designated disability/mental-illness P&A nonprofits meeting (2)(b)(i)-(iii) (MI-0043). Discount must be fully noted on the itemization; ineligibility reason must be stated specifically in the written response. No purpose statement required of ordinary requesters; fee/deposit challenges route through § 15.240a.

resolutions.unit: percent reduction of the labor-cost charges (labor components only)
resolutions.source_language: Reduce the charges for labor costs otherwise permitted under this section by 5% for each day the public body exceeds the time permitted under section 5(2) for a response to the request, with a maximum 50% reduction, if either of the following applies: (i) The late response was willful and intentional. (ii) The written request included language that conveyed a request for information within the first 250 words of the body of a letter, facsimile, electronic mail, or electronic mail attachment, or specifically included the words, characters, or abbreviations for "freedom of information", "information", "FOIA", "copy", or a recognizable misspelling of such, or appropriate legal code reference for this act, on the front of an envelope, or in the subject line of an electronic mail, letter, or facsimile cover page.
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Partial forfeiture, not full: applies only to labor charges, and only if the untimely response was willful and intentional OR the request carried the FOIA-flagging language/keywords of (9)(a)(ii). The reduction must be fully noted on the detailed itemization ((9)(b)).

resolutions.source_language: Subject to subsection (12), after a public body has granted and fulfilled a written request from an individual under this act, if the public body has not been paid in full the total amount under subsection (1) for the copies of public records that the public body made available to the individual as a result of that written request, the public body may require a deposit of up to 100% of the estimated fee before it begins a full public record search for any subsequent written request from that individual if all of the following apply:
resolutions.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
resolutions.notes: Michigan's only repeat-request fee mechanisms: (1) up-to-100% deposit for subsequent requests from a prior non-payer while all six (11)(a)-(f) conditions hold, expiring on proof of payment, later payment in full, or 365 days after the unpaid request ((12), MI-0057); (2) the indigent $20 discount is limited to twice per calendar year per public body ((2)(a)(i)) - a per-requestor-period counter. No aggregation-of-requests threshold and no carry-forward of fees across requests.

new_rules.legal_concept: Paper copies on other than 8-1/2x11 / 8-1/2x14 paper - actual incremental duplication cost
new_rules.atomic_rule: Paper copies on paper other than 8-1/2 x 11 or 8-1/2 x 14 inches are charged at the actual total incremental cost of necessary duplication or publication, not including labor, calculated and itemized as a total cost per sheet; the 10-cent cap applies only to the two named sizes.
new_rules.trigger: Paper copies provided on paper sizes other than 8-1/2 x 11 or 8-1/2 x 14 inches (oversized/nonstandard).
new_rules.source_language: For paper copies of public records provided to the requestor, the actual total incremental cost of necessary duplication or publication, not including labor. The cost of paper copies shall be calculated as a total cost per sheet of paper and shall be itemized and noted in a manner that expresses both the cost per sheet and the number of sheets provided. The fee must not exceed 10 cents per sheet of paper for copies of public records made on 8-1/2- by 11-inch paper or 8-1/2- by 14-inch paper.
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Am. 2020 PA 38; MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026, no 2024-2026 amendment)
new_rules.notes: Fills the oversized/nonstandard gap: the per-sheet 10-cent ceiling (MI-0038) is textually limited to letter/legal sizes; all other paper sizes stay under the actual-total-incremental-cost clause with mandatory per-sheet itemization. Amends nothing; complements MI-0038.

new_rules.legal_concept: State minimum hourly wage rate (external figure for the 6x contracted-redaction-labor cap)
new_rules.atomic_rule: The state minimum hourly wage rate referenced by MCL 15.234(1)(b)'s contracted-redaction-labor cap (6x that rate) is $12.48 beginning February 21, 2025, $13.73 beginning January 1, 2026, and $15.00 beginning January 1, 2027, with treasurer-calculated CPI adjustments published each October beginning October 2027 - making the contracted-labor ceiling $82.38/hour during 2026.
new_rules.trigger: Public body charges contracted labor for separating/deleting exempt information under MCL 15.234(1)(b) (no capable employee, FOIA-coordinator determined, contractor named on itemization).
new_rules.source_language: (1) Subject to the exceptions specified in this act, the minimum hourly wage rate is: (a) Beginning February 21, 2025, $12.48. (b) Beginning January 1, 2026, $13.73. (c) Beginning January 1, 2027, $15.00.
new_rules.source_authority: Mich. Comp. Laws § 408.934(1) (Improved Workforce Opportunity Wage Act, 2018 PA 337)
new_rules.effective_status: Current (Am. 2025 PA 1, imd. eff. Feb. 21, 2025; original initiative revived per Mothering Justice v Attorney General, No. 165325 (Mich. July 31, 2024)); $13.73 step effective Jan 1, 2026; $15.00 step Jan 1, 2027; CPI-adjusted thereafter unless state unemployment >= 8.5%
new_rules.notes: Delegation instrument for MI-0036's 6x cap - a moving external figure. 6 x $13.73 = $82.38/hour through Dec 31, 2026; becomes 6 x $15.00 = $90.00/hour on Jan 1, 2027. Opened at legislature.mi.gov (MCL complete through PA 91 of 2026).

applicability_notes: Michigan FOIA (1976 PA 442) binds all public bodies under one fee regime - MCL 15.232 defines public body to include a city, village, township, county, or other local governing body; every figure in this file therefore applies_to all_public_bodies unless noted.

The DTMB standard fee-itemization form referenced in MCL 15.234(4) is created for state agencies; 'other public bodies may use a form created by the department of technology, management, and budget or create a form of their own that complies with this subsection' - an optional model, not a municipal mandate, and it carries no fee figures.
The contracted-redaction-labor cap (6x state minimum wage) is a moving figure: $82.38/hour in 2026, $90.00/hour from Jan 1, 2027, CPI-adjusted afterward.
The fringe-benefit multiplier above 50% is available only in the § 15.234(5) website-then-paper scenario, capped at actual costs of providing the stipulated format.
material_negatives: No graduated page bands - a single flat 10-cent/sheet ceiling on letter/legal paper.
No free-page allowance, free labor hours per request, or periodic per-requestor free personnel time (the $20 waiver is category-specific, dollar-denominated).
No revised-estimate (% overrun) trigger, no estimate validity period, and no overrun re-issue/collection-block rule.
No de-minimis floor and no minimum fee; the structure is ceiling-only.
No certification fee, no AV per-recording/per-minute rates, and no commercial-purpose fee schedule anywhere in the act.
The § 15.235(2) response clock is never tolled for fees or deposits; after a deposit demand only a nonbinding best-efforts timeframe estimate governs production timing.

The 105% figure in § 15.234(11)(a) is a prior-request eligibility condition for the 100% deposit tool, not a revision-notice threshold - flagged because the machine-derived prior offered it for estimate items.
